glossary.definition: Fasting, specifically the obligatory fast during Ramadan. One of the Five Pillars of Islam.
The pre-dawn meal eaten before beginning the daily fast. It's a blessed meal and highly recommended.
The meal eaten to break the fast at sunset. Traditionally starts with dates and water.
The ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar. The month of obligatory fasting and spiritual reflection.
The sunset prayer, marking the end of the fasting period each day and time to break the fast.
The dawn prayer, marking the beginning of the fasting period for the day.
Special nightly prayers performed during Ramadan after Isha prayer. Usually involves reciting the entire Quran.
The Night of Power/Decree. Falls in the last ten nights of Ramadan and is considered better than a thousand months.
The Festival of Breaking the Fast, celebrated at the end of Ramadan. A day of joy, prayer, and community.
Obligatory charity, one of the Five Pillars. Often given during Ramadan. Typically 2.5% of wealth.
Voluntary charity given for the pleasure of Allah. Can be given at any time in any amount.
Supplication or prayer to Allah. A personal conversation with God, made at any time.
The holy book of Islam, believed to be the word of Allah revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
Sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), recorded as guidance for Muslims.
The practices and traditions of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Following Sunnah is highly encouraged.
The time to stop eating before Fajr. Usually a few minutes before the Fajr prayer call.
Intention. The intention to fast must be made before dawn for the fast to be valid.
The White Days - the 13th, 14th, and 15th of each Islamic month. Voluntary fasting on these days is recommended.
Excellence in worship, doing beautiful deeds. Worshipping Allah as though you see Him.
God-consciousness, piety, being mindful of Allah. Fasting helps develop taqwa.
